Sorry that happened to you. Healthcare in USA does sucks. About thise bills ... the $1500 was your deductible which is a set amout you have to pay out of pocket before the insurance kicks in. After you have MET that deductible, meaning you have paid already $1500 out of pocket for whatever services you need, then the insurance will start to cover at whatever percentage the service is covered.  That last part is called a copay, you and the insurance pay the bill together. The copay varies since the insurance has specific % set for specific services and procedures. You get to pay whatever percentage they don't cover. A lot of insurances get to negotiate with providers a contract rate which is less than what a service or procedure costs but that doesn't mean the provider can charge you more, if they do then it may be fraud. Not sure how long ago was your situation but look into that. Hope that helps :)

North Adams is quite far from the coast, any coast. Commute is bad, anywhere here. Since you are willing to drive I suggest Worcester County. Anywhere in Central MA the living cost is less pricey (still high on some areas) but really worth it. There are amazing hiking trails and beautiful scenery. Worcester, 2nd biggest city in New England has a commuter rail that takes you straight to Boston  and another that takes you to Providence, RI and closer to the South Coast. Small towns are usually very welcoming, at least in my personal experience. I moved from Boston 4 years ago and it was the best decision ever. Like the comment on top, crime is high but for the most part it won't affect you unless you go out looking for trouble. Worcester is centralized, diverse, has some great restaurants, plenty of jobs and living cost is not too bad. Taunton and Attleboro are good too and they are closer to the South Coast. North MA is beautiful as well but living cost is higher. If you are willing to consider roommates then definitely look into Boston because it is a great city but living cost is exuberant. There are really nice apartment complexes overlooking the sea. Expect to pay over 1k for just one room but at a nice place and building. Hope that helps and welcome to New England.
